description: Issue #839: at RUN TIME a profile keyword is a built-in name unconditionally. `execute()` has no active profile set — it runs every profile's primitives and the reader recognises all six block heads regardless of profile — so the declaration-slot guard cannot be gated on one, and `spec/grammar.md:408` says it must not be: "a name that could be declared in one implementation but not in another would be invisible and unpredictable to a learner". So `define ask` halts at phase-1 registration with `ol-reserved-word` and the `ask` call on line 4 never runs. A corpus that checks a rule at one stage does not cover it at the other — keep an executing case for any rule both stages implement. `check()` and `execute()` reach that answer through one predicate, `@openlogo/parser`'s `isBuiltInName`, rather than composing it each; `packages/parser/src/built-in-names.test.mjs` and the Core-only fixture `core-language/check/reserved-word-profile-names-under-core-alone` pin the two sides against it. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists and still runs — under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — and is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy does not appear beside the check's. The other findings recorded here are independent faults in the same program, each reported once.
